evidence.title: Autonomous emergency braking optimal coordination control strategy for commercial buses considering safety and comfort.
evidence.abstract: The traditional dual-stage warning and dual-grade braking autonomous emergency braking (AEB) control strategy has sudden change in the expected braking deceleration during the switch of working state, which will easily lead to significant longitudinal jerk of the vehicle and affect ride comfort during emergency braking. To solve this problem, an AEB optimal control strategy considering coordination safety and comfort is proposed. First, an in improved Time-To-Collision pre-estimation model was designed, and the AEB state threshold time determination method was proposed by combining vehicle braking process and driver emergency braking characteristics. Second, an AEB hierarchical control strategy was designed, the upper layer designed an expected braking deceleration optimal decision controller based on particle swarm optimization linear quadratic regulator (PSO-LQR), and introduced a comfort time compensation coefficient to rectification the PSO-LQR controller. Moreover, an expected braking deceleration tracking controller based on feedforward and robust integral sliding mode feedback control was designed in the lower layer. Next, an AEB software architecture based on AUTOSAR was designed to enhance the standardization of control strategy software code generation. Finally, the Hardware-in-the-loop test and real vehicle experimental results indicate that the proposed AEB optimal coordination control strategy can meet the safety requirements of emergency collision avoidance functions, and effectively reduce the longitudinal jerk compared to the traditional AEB control strategy, it significantly improves the ride comfort of commercial buses during emergency braking processes.

evidence.title: Making Ends Meet or Just Meeting at the Ends? Assessing End-to-End Distance in Folded RNA Sequences and Other Branched Structures.
evidence.abstract: Researchers have repeatedly found that the ends of an RNA sequence are significantly closer than expected for a random linear chain. However, we prove that the ends of a branched structure are almost certainly close. Our results are obtained via combinatorial branching models of increasing complexity using tools from multivariate analytic combinatorics. We completely characterize parameters tracking end-to-end distance, including means and variances. Then, we compare to existing datasets of known RNA structures, as well as the minimum free-energy structures of randomized shuffles. We find that the shuffled structures resemble our theoretical distributions while the known RNA structures have similar parameter values but are more concentrated. The helices on the exterior loop of a structure draw the ends of the sequence together, and we find evidence that these helices are more stable than expected when compared to their counterparts in uniformly random branched structures.

evidence.title: Process Optimization and Performance Evaluation of CuCrZr Alloy Deposited by Blue-Near-Infrared Hybrid Laser Directed Energy Deposition.
evidence.abstract: The high thermal conductivity and low initial near-infrared laser absorptivity of T2 pure copper hinder stable deposition of compositionally similar CuCrZr alloys. This study deposited CuCrZr on T2 copper using hybrid blue and near-infrared laser directed energy deposition, targeting 15% dilution. Single-factor experiments established the process window; Taguchi orthogonal experiments, signal-to-noise ratio analysis, and analysis of variance identified optimized parameters. Independent replicates and microstructural and performance characterization verified the optimization. FLOW-3D simulations supported analysis of deposit formation and interfacial fusion. Scanning speed and hatching distance were the main factors affecting dilution within the investigated window. The optimized near-infrared laser power, powder feed rate, scanning speed, and hatching distance were 2700 W, 12 g/min, 18 mm/s, and 0.7 mm, respectively. Validation experiments yielded 14.81% mean dilution, with complete deposit cross-sections and continuous interfaces. CT measurements indicated approximately 99.99% relative density in specimens deposited using these parameters. Compared with the substrate, mean microhardness increased by 15.90%, mean friction coefficient decreased by 20.5%, and wear volume and specific wear rate both decreased by 49.9%. This study provides a process basis for stable CuCrZr deposition and surface strengthening on pure copper.

evidence.title: Genomic microdiversity of Mycobacterium africanum in Sénégal.
evidence.abstract: Introduction Mycobacterium africanum is responsible for up to half of tuberculosis cases in West Africa and comprises four sub lineages. Its genomic diversity remains undescribed in Sénégal where M. africanum was first described and where the present study was conducted. Results Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) identified one M. africanum lineage L5 isolate and 50 M. africanum lineage L6 isolates, with a predominance of sub lineage L6.1.1 (24/50, 43.7%) across seven of eight regions of Sénégal. The Dakar region gathered all the sub lineages (L5.3, L6.1, L6.1.1, L6.1.3, L6.2.3, L6.3.1, L6.3.2, L6.3.3, unclassified L6), except for sub lineage L6.2. Further Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) analysis revealed substantial genetic diversity among the lineage L6 isolates with mean value of 668.54 (±239.61), while themedian was 465 SNPs (interquartile range = 400, median absolute deviation:163.09). According to the World health Organization Catalogue of mutations in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance, WGS predicted antibiotic resistance in 16 strains. Comparing Drug Susceptibility Testing (DST) and WGS results showed complete concordance across 19 DST tested strains. Conclusion This study highlights the diversity of M. africanum in Sénégal, with intra-lineage genomic variability and predicted antimicrobial resistance. The presence of synonymous mutations in the absence of resistance-associated variants suggests that WGS-based predictions of drug resistance should be interpreted with caution.

evidence.abstract: Purpose This study investigated the non-linear, time-dependent alterations in cardiorespiratory fitness, running economy (RE), and metabolic kinetics during the first week of acute exposure to a sub-high altitude (1,300 m) in elite youth endurance athletes. Maximal oxygen uptake ( V˙O2max ), peak running speed ( vV˙O2max ), and submaximal RE (steady-state V˙O2 at 12, 14, and 16 km·h - ¹) were assessed using an automated metabolic cart. Blood lactate concentration ([La - ]b) and maximal heart rate (HRmax) were measured. Daily waking morning heart rate (morning HR) and resting arterial oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) were continuously monitored. evidence.title: A Static and Dynamic Combined Center of Mass Measurement Method Based on Multi-View Vision.
evidence.abstract: The position of the center of mass directly affects the attitude control and flight safety of moving bodies such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Therefore, high-precision measurement of the center of mass is required. Existing methods require changing the posture of the measured object multiple times. This introduces repeated positioning errors and suffers from poor equipment versatility. To address these issues, this paper proposes a static and dynamic combined measurement method for the center of mass based on multi-view vision. First, the relationship between the swing period and the pendulum length under the simple pendulum principle is analyzed. The basic principle of determining the direction of the center of mass using the line of gravity is also examined. Second, an under-constrained compound pendulum fixture is designed. A binocular vision system is used to track circular markers, perform FFT-based period verification, and fit the gravity line using singular value decomposition (SVD). Third, using a standard cubic iron block as the test object, the influence of pendulum length and swing angle on measurement accuracy is studied. Finally, experiments verify that the proposed method can obtain three-dimensional coordinates of the center of mass under a single suspension condition. The results show that with a pendulum length of 330 mm and an initial swing angle of 4°, the root mean square error of the center of mass measurement is 0.70 mm, and the maximum deviation over five repeated measurements is 1.45 mm. This method does not require repeated lifting or changes in posture. It can meet the need for in-situ, high-precision center of mass measurement of UAVs and other aircraft.

evidence.title: Impact of Power on Uneven Development: Evaluating Built-Up Area Changes in Chengdu Based on NPP-VIIRS Images (2015–2019)
evidence.abstract: In the context of uneven development studies of China, urban built-up area changes are the index of the impact of power, as the local government is the only party that is able to acquire agricultural land and convert it to construction urban land. Existing studies generally use statistical data to describe the built-up area changes and struggle to meet the requirement of an updated and inexpensive monitoring of uneven development, especially for western cities with tight budgets. Open access NPP-VIIRS (Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite), NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), and nighttime LST (Land Surface Temperature) data ranging from 2015 to 2019 were analyzed with a stratified SVM (Support Vector Machine) method in this study to track urban built-up area changes in Chengdu, one of the biggest cities in Western China. The SDE (Standard Deviation Ellipse) and Moran’s I were then applied to evaluate the spatial variations of the built-up area changes. It was revealed that the spatial evolution of built-up area change in Chengdu over the period 2015–2019 demonstrated a “northwest-southeast” spatial expansion pattern, and the change distance in the center of gravity in 2018 and 2019 was greater than that from 2015 to 2017, which reflected the faster uneven development in 2018 and 2019 in Chengdu. The results were verified with finer resolution Landsat-8 OLI images; the high OA (all larger than 92%) and KAPPA (all larger than 0.6) values showed the accuracy of the method. The methodology proposed in this study offers a practical way for cities with tight budgets to monitor uneven development, and this study suggests a further adaption using higher-resolution remote sensing images and field experiments.

evidence.title: Structural distance to the tRNA-synthetase binding interface predicts pathogenicity but is captured by AlphaMissense and EVE.
evidence.abstract: Variants of uncertain significance have accumulated as genomic sequencing has become more widespread, which complicates rare disease diagnosis and requires substantial resources for re-evaluation. Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARSs) are a protein family with extensive variant data and well-characterized disease associations, making them an ideal system for investigating the relationship between variant location and pathogenicity. Using structural distance measurements to the ARS-tRNA binding interface combined with existing pathogenicity predictors, AlphaMissense and EVE, we investigated whether explicit structural binding information could improve missense variant pathogenicity prediction. Pathogenic variants were found to cluster significantly closer to the tRNA-binding interface than benign variants (p = 1.3e-09). Incorporating explicit distance information into a Bayesian mixture model did not substantially improve predictive performance over AlphaMissense and EVE alone. This suggests that these models already implicitly capture relevant structural binding context. However, a clinically important subset of interface variants classified as ambiguous by both existing models identifies a specific gap where explicit structural distance information may provide added discriminative value. However our analysis revealed that structural distance alone does not meaningfully contribute in prediction of pathogenicity for these variants. Incorporating additional biologically relevant features not captured by existing models, such as protein stability or conformational dynamics, as well as refining structural distance calculations, may further improve classification of this subset. These findings highlight both the power and the limitations of existing pathogenicity predictors and suggest that structurally informed approaches targeting the binding interface in addiition to other features represent a promising direction for improving classification of these ambiguous variants that have great clinical significance.

evidence.title: Research on the impact of transceiver isolation of GB-SAR on imaging quality.
evidence.abstract: Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GB-SAR) systems frequently suffer from insufficient transceiver isolation due to their compact architecture. This insufficiency leads to transmitted signal leakage into the receiving channel, generating third-order intermodulation distortion (IM3). Consequently, the imaging signal to noise ratio (SNR) is degraded and artifacts in the range direction are introduced. Utilizing an independently developed Ku-band GB-SAR system termed S-SAR M, this study explores the influence mechanism of transceiver isolation on imaging quality through dynamic adjustment of antenna spatial parameters. It identifies a system-specific critical isolation threshold and an optimal design range, thereby offering a theoretical basis and practical guidelines for hardware optimization of GB-SAR systems. The isolation model is quantitatively calibrated against the measured horn radiation pattern and antenna geometry with a root-mean-square error of 1.8 dB, and the critical threshold is derived analytically from receiver nonlinearity parameters through the third-order input intercept point (IIP3). The results indicate that antenna angle is the dominant factor for isolation improvement, with an average enhancement of 56.3 percent achieved as the angle increases from 0 to 60 degrees. Antenna separation exhibits a synergistic effect on isolation at larger angles. A critical isolation threshold of 74 dB is established to suppress range artifacts induced by IM3 in the S-SAR M system; below this threshold, artifacts consistently occur. Moreover, a tri-segmented nonlinear relationship between isolation and SNR is observed, with an optimal balance region located between 74 dB and 80 dB where the peak SNR is maintained. One-way analysis of variance delivers a result with p less than 0.001 and confirms the significance of these trends. A quantitative artifact-to-background energy ratio further corroborates the visual artifact classification. These findings offer important insights for enhancing the performance of GB-SAR systems. It should be noted that the reported numerical thresholds are specific to the S-SAR M hardware configuration; a normalized isolation-margin framework is therefore provided to transfer the methodology, with platform-specific calibration, to GB-SAR systems using other frequency bands or receiver architectures.

evidence.title: Feasibility of using a mobile cardiotocograph device in an ambulance during maternal transport.
evidence.abstract: Maternal transfer generally refers to the emergency transportation of a pregnant woman to a medical facility with more advanced capabilities when her condition, or that of the fetus, deteriorates or is expected to deteriorate, thereby ensuring the safety of both mother and fetus. This procedure is frequently performed in Japan, where childbirth at primary obstetric facilities is common. However, no reports have described attempts to remotely monitor maternal and fetal vital signs inside an ambulance during transport and use these data to support clinical care at a remote location. The current study aimed to assess the feasibility of a system that enables real-time remote monitoring (RM) using a small mobile cardiotocograph (CTG) in an ambulance during maternal transport from primary obstetric facilities to a higher-level perinatal medical center. This study included women with singleton pregnancies beyond 22 weeks of gestation who were transferred from nine private clinics to a university hospital because of medical complications. Using a small mobile CTG device, the CTG data were transmitted during maternal transfer to a university hospital. The obstetrician of the university hospital checked the data in real-time using tablets to select the appropriate treatment. A questionnaire survey was conducted on the medical staff of the primary facilities who accompanied the patients during maternal transport. An online survey was also administered to paramedics only after the recruitment period. The study period was from August 2021 to August 2023. In total, 68 pregnant women were enrolled in this study and analyzed. The median time from getting into the ambulance to arrival at the university hospital was 34.5 (range: 15.0-67.0) min. No monitoring sessions were discontinued because of connectivity issues. All 68 fetal heart rate records were legible, and the median proportion of the total legible period in each recording was 91.1% (range: 53.9%-99.8%). FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. custody_records.raw_content: Researchers have repeatedly found that the ends of an RNA sequence are significantly closer than expected for a random linear chain. However, we prove that the ends of a branched structure are almost certainly close. Our results are obtained via combinatorial branching models of increasing complexity using tools from multivariate analytic combinatorics. We completely characterize parameters tracking end-to-end distance, including means and variances. Then, we compare to existing datasets of known RNA structures, as well as the minimum free-energy structures of randomized shuffles. We find that the shuffled structures resemble our theoretical distributions while the known RNA structures have similar parameter values but are more concentrated. The helices on the exterior loop of a structure draw the ends of the sequence together, and we find evidence that these helices are more stable than expected when compared to their counterparts in uniformly random branched structures.

custody_records.raw_content: The high thermal conductivity and low initial near-infrared laser absorptivity of T2 pure copper hinder stable deposition of compositionally similar CuCrZr alloys. This study deposited CuCrZr on T2 copper using hybrid blue and near-infrared laser directed energy deposition, targeting 15% dilution. Single-factor experiments established the process window; Taguchi orthogonal experiments, signal-to-noise ratio analysis, and analysis of variance identified optimized parameters. Independent replicates and microstructural and performance characterization verified the optimization. FLOW-3D simulations supported analysis of deposit formation and interfacial fusion. Scanning speed and hatching distance were the main factors affecting dilution within the investigated window. The optimized near-infrared laser power, powder feed rate, scanning speed, and hatching distance were 2700 W, 12 g/min, 18 mm/s, and 0.7 mm, respectively. Validation experiments yielded 14.81% mean dilution, with complete deposit cross-sections and continuous interfaces. CT measurements indicated approximately 99.99% relative density in specimens deposited using these parameters. Compared with the substrate, mean microhardness increased by 15.90%, mean friction coefficient decreased by 20.5%, and wear volume and specific wear rate both decreased by 49.9%. This study provides a process basis for stable CuCrZr deposition and surface strengthening on pure copper.

Its genomic diversity remains undescribed in Sénégal where M. africanum was first described and where the present study was conducted. Results Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) identified one M. africanum lineage L5 isolate and 50 M. africanum lineage L6 isolates, with a predominance of sub lineage L6.1.1 (24/50, 43.7%) across seven of eight regions of Sénégal. The Dakar region gathered all the sub lineages (L5.3, L6.1, L6.1.1, L6.1.3, L6.2.3, L6.3.1, L6.3.2, L6.3.3, unclassified L6), except for sub lineage L6.2. According to the World health Organization Catalogue of mutations in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance, WGS predicted antibiotic resistance in 16 strains. Comparing Drug Susceptibility Testing (DST) and WGS results showed complete concordance across 19 DST tested strains. The presence of synonymous mutations in the absence of resistance-associated variants suggests that WGS-based predictions of drug resistance should be interpreted with caution.

custody_records.raw_content: The position of the center of mass directly affects the attitude control and flight safety of moving bodies such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Therefore, high-precision measurement of the center of mass is required. Existing methods require changing the posture of the measured object multiple times. This introduces repeated positioning errors and suffers from poor equipment versatility. To address these issues, this paper proposes a static and dynamic combined measurement method for the center of mass based on multi-view vision. First, the relationship between the swing period and the pendulum length under the simple pendulum principle is analyzed. The basic principle of determining the direction of the center of mass using the line of gravity is also examined. Second, an under-constrained compound pendulum fixture is designed. A binocular vision system is used to track circular markers, perform FFT-based period verification, and fit the gravity line using singular value decomposition (SVD). Third, using a standard cubic iron block as the test object, the influence of pendulum length and swing angle on measurement accuracy is studied. Finally, experiments verify that the proposed method can obtain three-dimensional coordinates of the center of mass under a single suspension condition. The results show that with a pendulum length of 330 mm and an initial swing angle of 4°, the root mean square error of the center of mass measurement is 0.70 mm, and the maximum deviation over five repeated measurements is 1.45 mm. This method does not require repeated lifting or changes in posture. It can meet the need for in-situ, high-precision center of mass measurement of UAVs and other aircraft.

custody_records.raw_content: In the context of uneven development studies of China, urban built-up area changes are the index of the impact of power, as the local government is the only party that is able to acquire agricultural land and convert it to construction urban land. Existing studies generally use statistical data to describe the built-up area changes and struggle to meet the requirement of an updated and inexpensive monitoring of uneven development, especially for western cities with tight budgets. Open access NPP-VIIRS (Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite), NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), and nighttime LST (Land Surface Temperature) data ranging from 2015 to 2019 were analyzed with a stratified SVM (Support Vector Machine) method in this study to track urban built-up area changes in Chengdu, one of the biggest cities in Western China. The SDE (Standard Deviation Ellipse) and Moran’s I were then applied to evaluate the spatial variations of the built-up area changes. It was revealed that the spatial evolution of built-up area change in Chengdu over the period 2015–2019 demonstrated a “northwest-southeast” spatial expansion pattern, and the change distance in the center of gravity in 2018 and 2019 was greater than that from 2015 to 2017, which reflected the faster uneven development in 2018 and 2019 in Chengdu. The results were verified with finer resolution Landsat-8 OLI images; the high OA (all larger than 92%) and KAPPA (all larger than 0.6) values showed the accuracy of the method. The methodology proposed in this study offers a practical way for cities with tight budgets to monitor uneven development, and this study suggests a further adaption using higher-resolution remote sensing images and field experiments.

custody_records.raw_content: Variants of uncertain significance have accumulated as genomic sequencing has become more widespread, which complicates rare disease diagnosis and requires substantial resources for re-evaluation. Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (ARSs) are a protein family with extensive variant data and well-characterized disease associations, making them an ideal system for investigating the relationship between variant location and pathogenicity. Using structural distance measurements to the ARS-tRNA binding interface combined with existing pathogenicity predictors, AlphaMissense and EVE, we investigated whether explicit structural binding information could improve missense variant pathogenicity prediction. Pathogenic variants were found to cluster significantly closer to the tRNA-binding interface than benign variants (p = 1.3e-09). Incorporating explicit distance information into a Bayesian mixture model did not substantially improve predictive performance over AlphaMissense and EVE alone. This suggests that these models already implicitly capture relevant structural binding context. However, a clinically important subset of interface variants classified as ambiguous by both existing models identifies a specific gap where explicit structural distance information may provide added discriminative value. However our analysis revealed that structural distance alone does not meaningfully contribute in prediction of pathogenicity for these variants. Incorporating additional biologically relevant features not captured by existing models, such as protein stability or conformational dynamics, as well as refining structural distance calculations, may further improve classification of this subset. These findings highlight both the power and the limitations of existing pathogenicity predictors and suggest that structurally informed approaches targeting the binding interface in addiition to other features represent a promising direction for improving classification of these ambiguous variants that have great clinical significance.

custody_records.raw_content: Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GB-SAR) systems frequently suffer from insufficient transceiver isolation due to their compact architecture. This insufficiency leads to transmitted signal leakage into the receiving channel, generating third-order intermodulation distortion (IM3). Consequently, the imaging signal to noise ratio (SNR) is degraded and artifacts in the range direction are introduced. Utilizing an independently developed Ku-band GB-SAR system termed S-SAR M, this study explores the influence mechanism of transceiver isolation on imaging quality through dynamic adjustment of antenna spatial parameters. It identifies a system-specific critical isolation threshold and an optimal design range, thereby offering a theoretical basis and practical guidelines for hardware optimization of GB-SAR systems. The isolation model is quantitatively calibrated against the measured horn radiation pattern and antenna geometry with a root-mean-square error of 1.8 dB, and the critical threshold is derived analytically from receiver nonlinearity parameters through the third-order input intercept point (IIP3). The results indicate that antenna angle is the dominant factor for isolation improvement, with an average enhancement of 56.3 percent achieved as the angle increases from 0 to 60 degrees. Antenna separation exhibits a synergistic effect on isolation at larger angles. A critical isolation threshold of 74 dB is established to suppress range artifacts induced by IM3 in the S-SAR M system; below this threshold, artifacts consistently occur. Moreover, a tri-segmented nonlinear relationship between isolation and SNR is observed, with an optimal balance region located between 74 dB and 80 dB where the peak SNR is maintained. One-way analysis of variance delivers a result with p less than 0.001 and confirms the significance of these trends. A quantitative artifact-to-background energy ratio further corroborates the visual artifact classification. These findings offer important insights for enhancing the performance of GB-SAR systems. It should be noted that the reported numerical thresholds are specific to the S-SAR M hardware configuration; a normalized isolation-margin framework is therefore provided to transfer the methodology, with platform-specific calibration, to GB-SAR systems using other frequency bands or receiver architectures.
